actions.name: Review completed MRI safety screening paper form
actions.result: Form submitted at check-in: patient answered 'No' to all implant/device questions, 'No' to prior metal injury, 'No' to claustrophobia. Signed and dated today.

actions.name: Verify patient identity and imaging order
actions.result: Patient confirms name Dale Hutchins, DOB on file, and states he is here for a back scan. Order in RIS: MRI lumbar spine without and with gadolinium contrast, ordered by Dr. Patel for radiculopathy/suspected spinal stenosis, prior lumbar fusion.

actions.name: Direct screening interview for metal/implants (go beyond paper form)
actions.result: On direct questioning patient discloses: spinal fusion hardware (2014), left total knee replacement, transdermal fentanyl patch currently on right upper arm, large tattoo sleeve on left arm. No mention of any eye injury history at this point.

actions.name: Occupational metal-exposure screening
actions.result: Patient reports 20+ years as a pipe welder/metal fabricator; grinds and welds metal regularly. When asked generally about eye protection he says 'yeah I wear the goggles,' downplaying the topic.

actions.name: Camera inspection of medication patch
actions.result: Visual inspection via video shows an intact transdermal patch on the right upper arm; patient confirms it is prescribed fentanyl for chronic back pain. Technologist notes patch has a metallic foil backing.

actions.name: Camera inspection of skin for tattoos near scan field
actions.result: Visual inspection shows a tattoo sleeve covering the left arm from shoulder to wrist; no visible tattoo markings over the lumbar spine region on camera. Patient denies any swelling, burning, or redness in tattooed skin with prior MRI exposure.

actions.name: Review surgical/implant history in chart
actions.result: 2014 operative note: posterior lumbar fusion L4-S1 with titanium pedicle screws and rods, hardware vendor/model not specified in available records.

actions.name: Review most recent renal function (eGFR) for contrast safety
actions.result: eGFR 52 mL/min/1.73m2 (2 months ago), mildly reduced (Stage 3a CKD range). No prior gadolinium reaction on file.

actions.name: Check for documented contrast allergy
actions.result: Allergy list reviewed: No known drug or contrast allergies documented.

actions.name: Claustrophobia and anxiety screening
actions.result: Patient reports one prior MRI during which he panicked, asked to be pulled out partway through. Minimizes it today, saying he's 'probably fine now' and does not mention any plan for today's exam.

actions.name: Review home blood glucose/diabetes control
actions.result: Chart notes type 2 diabetes diagnosed 2016, managed with metformin 1000 mg twice daily; last HbA1c 7.4% three months ago.

actions.name: Review MRI order for consistency with clinical indication
actions.result: Order and chart are consistent: lumbar spine MRI without/with contrast for leg pain and suspected recurrent/adjacent-segment stenosis after 2014 fusion.

actions.name: Document findings and recommendations in technologist note for radiologist
actions.result: Note drafted flagging: (1) occupational metal exposure with history of ocular metallic foreign body removal and inconsistent eye protection — recommend orbit X-rays to rule out retained intraorbital metal before MRI; (2) known titanium lumbar hardware, model unconfirmed — generally MR-conditional but may need surgical records clarification and will cause local artifact; (3) transdermal fentanyl patch must be removed immediately before scan and replaced per protocol after; (4) mild renal impairment (eGFR 52) — contrast dose/agent selection and metformin hold instructions to be confirmed with radiologist/ordering provider; (5) significant claustrophobia history with planned non-disclosure — recommend addressing accommodations (coaching, open MRI, or sedation referral) before proceeding.

mismatches.patientClaim: Patient states he already completed the paper screening form and marked 'no' to all implant, metal, patch, and claustrophobia questions, implying there's nothing further to discuss.
mismatches.recordEvidence: The completed form (d1) shows blanket 'No' answers to every safety question, directly contradicted by what the direct interview later reveals (fusion hardware, knee replacement, fentanyl patch, prior scanner panic).
mismatches.teachingPoint: Self-administered paper screening forms are frequently incomplete or inaccurate; a structured verbal interview by the technologist is required before every MRI, especially when occupational or surgical history suggests risk.

mismatches.patientClaim: Patient downplays his prior panic episode and does not mention any plan for how he'll handle today's scan.
mismatches.recordEvidence: Outside facility technologist note (d6) documents that three years ago the patient's MRI was aborted after about 4 minutes due to severe panic, and that he never followed up on the recommended anti-anxiety premedication.
mismatches.teachingPoint: A patient's casual minimization of claustrophobia does not reliably predict tolerance of a lengthy contrast-enhanced lumbar MRI; documented history of an aborted exam should prompt proactive, direct, rapport-building questioning about his actual plan and discussion of accommodations rather than relying on surface-level reassurance.

objectives.text: Recognize that a self-reported paper MRI safety form may be inaccurate and conduct a thorough verbal screening interview that uncovers undisclosed implants, devices, and metal exposure history.

Identify occupational metallic foreign body risk through welding/grinding history, and through direct, sensitive, rapport-building questioning uncover a prior ocular metal injury and inconsistent eye protection use; know to flag the patient for orbit X-rays before MRI to rule out retained intraorbital metal.

Correctly manage a known MR-conditional implant (spinal fusion hardware, knee replacement) by recognizing it is generally safe but requires documentation of model/manufacturer and anticipation of imaging artifact, and recommend obtaining outside records.
Identify and plan removal of a transdermal medication patch with metallic backing before scanning, and counsel on reapplication after the exam.

Review contrast-safety factors within technologist scope — renal function (eGFR), metformin use/timing, and allergy history — and recognize when findings must be escalated to the radiologist/ordering provider rather than decided independently.

Elicit a history of claustrophobia and a prior aborted MRI, recognize the patient's plan to not disclose this, and escalate for accommodation planning rather than allowing the patient to proceed unprepared.

scenario.studentBrief: You are a radiologic technology student performing a telehealth pre-imaging safety screening call with Dale Hutchins, 58, who is scheduled for a lumbar spine MRI without/with gadolinium contrast in 3 days. He has already submitted a paper screening form. Your job is to verify his identity and the order, conduct a thorough verbal MRI safety and contrast-risk screening beyond the paper form, inspect what you can by camera, and flag any concerns to the radiologist before the exam proceeds.
scenario.chiefComplaint: Pre-MRI safety screening for scheduled lumbar spine MRI with/without contrast, in a patient with leg pain and suspected spinal stenosis after prior fusion surgery.
scenario.openingLine: Hey there, I'm calling about my MRI I've got coming up for my back and this leg pain I've been having. I already filled out that form, so I think we're good to go.
tasks: Verify patient identity and confirm the imaging order.
Conduct a structured verbal MRI safety interview covering implants, devices, metal exposure, patches, and tattoos.
Screen for contrast-related risk factors including renal function, medication use, and allergy history.
Screen for prior MRI experience and scanner tolerance.
Document findings and escalate appropriate concerns to the radiologist before the scheduled exam.

profile.summary: "A 58-year-old welder completes a paper MRI safety form marked entirely 'no,' but a careful verbal screening interview by the radiologic technology student uncovers an undisclosed ocular metal injury with ongoing occupational exposure, known spinal and knee hardware, a metallic-backed fentanyl patch, mild renal impairment relevant to contrast, and a minimized history of claustrophobia with a prior aborted scan. The case teaches structured MRI safety screening, contrast-risk recognition, and appropriate escalation to the radiologist within the technologist's scope of practice."
profile.title: "Pre-MRI Safety Screening in a Welder with Undisclosed Metal Exposure and Claustrophobia"

answerKey.primaryProblem: Pre-imaging safety screening reveals multiple undisclosed risks before lumbar spine MRI with/without contrast: occupational metallic foreign body exposure with prior ocular metal injury, known MR-conditional spinal/knee hardware with unconfirmed model, a metallic-backed fentanyl patch, mild renal impairment relevant to gadolinium contrast and metformin, and unaddressed claustrophobia with a prior aborted MRI.
differential: Retained intraorbital metallic foreign body risk from welding/grinding exposure (requires orbit X-ray clearance before MRI)
MR-conditional spinal fusion and knee hardware (safe but needs model confirmation and artifact anticipation)
Metallic-backed transdermal patch requiring removal before scan
Mild renal impairment (eGFR 52) relevant to gadolinium-based contrast agent selection/dosing
Metformin timing/hold considerations around contrast administration per facility protocol
Claustrophobia/panic risk based on prior aborted MRI, unaddressed by patient
keyFindings: Paper screening form marked 'No' to all implant/metal/patch/claustrophobia questions, contradicted by verbal interview
20+ years welding/grinding with inconsistent eye protection and history of ER removal of ocular metal sliver ~15 years ago
Known L4-S1 titanium spinal fusion hardware (2014) and left total knee replacement, manufacturer/model unknown, outside records not yet obtained
Transdermal fentanyl patch 25 mcg/hr on right upper arm with metallic foil backing, not disclosed on form
eGFR 52 mL/min/1.73m2 two months ago (downtrending from 68 eighteen months ago), on metformin 1000 mg BID taken same-day
Prior MRI three years ago aborted at ~4 minutes due to panic; patient plans to not disclose and 'tough it out' this time
No known contrast, iodine, or shellfish allergy; no pacemaker or other implanted electronics
plan: Flag patient to radiologist for orbit X-ray screening prior to MRI given occupational metal exposure and history of ocular metallic foreign body

Document spinal fusion and knee hardware as MR-conditional; attempt to obtain outside operative records for manufacturer/model confirmation and alert radiologist to anticipated artifact near lumbar spine

Instruct patient to remove the fentanyl patch immediately before the scan and have a plan to reapply a new patch per prescriber instructions after the exam; do not improvise contrast or medication decisions as a technologist

Escalate renal function (eGFR 52) and metformin use to radiologist/ordering provider for contrast agent selection and any metformin-hold instructions per facility protocol; technologist does not independently decide to proceed or withhold contrast

Address claustrophobia proactively: discuss accommodation options (coaching/breathing techniques, open MRI referral, or sedation referral) with the patient and relay the prior aborted-exam history to the radiologist/scheduling team rather than letting the patient attempt the exam undisclosed
Correct and re-document the safety screening form findings in the chart so they are not lost before exam day
redFlags: Possible retained metallic intraorbital foreign body given occupational exposure and injury history — do not proceed to MRI without orbit X-ray clearance
Unconfirmed implant hardware model in a strong magnetic field environment
Risk of acute panic/inability to complete exam if claustrophobia is not proactively addressed
Mild renal impairment altering gadolinium contrast risk profile, requiring radiologist input rather than technologist decision
educationPoints: Verbal MRI safety screening by a trained technologist is essential even after a completed paper form, since patients often misunderstand or omit relevant history
Occupational metal exposure (welding/grinding) with any history of ocular metal injury warrants orbit imaging before MRI to exclude retained ferromagnetic foreign bodies
Known orthopedic/spinal hardware is usually MR-conditional, but documenting manufacturer/model and anticipating artifact is part of thorough screening
Transdermal patches with metallic backings must be removed before MRI and the plan for reapplication clarified with the prescribing provider

Renal function and metformin use are relevant to contrast safety, but final decisions about proceeding, withholding, or holding medication belong to the radiologist/ordering provider, not the technologist
Patients may minimize fear of the scanner out of pride; proactively screening for and normalizing accommodation options improves exam completion and patient safety
